# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 ✍ 👍 👎 👋 ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🖐 👍 👎]

## Thinking

I'm Deaf: I see the bomb and gestures, I hear nothing, I never receive anyone's speech. My speech reaches both Mute and Blind; my gestures reach only Mute. Critically, Mute's *only* output is gesture, and only I can see gestures — so I am the sole bridge from Mute's manual knowledge to Blind's hands. Everything must funnel through my voice.

What arrived this round: Mute gestured 🖐 ✍ 👍 👎 👋 ☝ and Blind gestured 👋 🖐 👍 👎. No code exists yet, but the overlap (👋 🖐 👍 👎) suggests near-universal signs: 🖐 likely "five" — which matches the five wires I can see and that Blind can presumably feel; ✍ likely "manual/writing"; ☝ possibly "one/display"; 👍 👎 as yes/no. I can't verify any of it, so I won't act on guesses — but I'll answer the most probable question (🖐 = five?) and mirror their own symbols back with answers attached.

The bomb, in full: display reads 3, one white light, five wires — white, red, green, blue, orange in positions 1–5.

Plan: broadcast the complete bomb description by voice (both can hear me). Propose an explicit gesture code for Mute — numbers as repeated ☝, 👍/👎 for yes/no, 👋 for repeat, module symbols — so next round Mute can gesture manual rules to me and I'll relay them to Blind aloud. Tell Blind to report tactiles by voice to Mute and by gesture to me, and to touch nothing decisive yet.

## Calls

```
speak(text="Both of you, hear me. I am the deaf one: I see the bomb and gestures, but I hear nothing, so your voices never reach me. The bomb in full: the display reads three. There is one light, and it is white. There are five wires. In order, one to five: white, red, green, blue, orange. That is everything printed on it. Blind: I cannot hear your voice, so reach me by gesture; Mute can hear you, so also describe what you feel out loud. Feel gently, but do not cut or press anything yet. Mute: I could not read your signs yet. You hear me, so let us fix a code. Numbers are ☝ repeated that many times, so ☝☝☝ means three. Yes is 👍, no is 👎. 👋 means repeat your last message. To ask about the bomb, send the module then the question: ☝ is the display, ✌ is the wires, 🤟 is the light. If your 🖐 meant five: yes, five wires, and Blind signed five back. Gesture me the manual's questions and I will answer and speak every instruction to Blind myself. Nobody acts until your rule reaches Blind through my voice. I have just gestured to you: ☝☝☝ three, 🖐 five, 👍 yes, 👋👍 light yes white.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝","☝","☝","🖐","👍","👋","👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ 🤟 ☝ ✌ ☝ 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🖐]

## Thinking

The rejection was purely addressing: `to="all"` names nobody. The fix is to drop the `to` parameter entirely — an unnamed call reaches everyone able to perceive it, which is exactly what this broadcast needs (both Mute and Blind can hear my voice). The content was sound: confirm the code, correct the wire count to five, assign position numbers to wires, inventory request for Blind, and open the Mute → me → Blind rule pipeline. I keep the same gesture to Mute, whose symbols (☝ 👍 🤟 ✌ 🖐 🤝) are all in the alphabet. Resubmitting the whole turn, corrected.

## Calls

```
speak(text="Mute, your signs came through perfectly in our code. I read them as: is the display three, and how many lights, and how many wires. Answers: yes, the display reads three. There is exactly one light, and it is white. But there are five wires, not one. Blind, your signs said yes, five. If your hands counted five wires by touch, then all three of us now agree on the bomb. Blind, here is the whole bomb so your fingers can match it: a display showing the number three, one light that is white, and five wires. In order from position one to position five the colors are: white, red, green, blue, orange. From now on everyone names wires by position number only: wire one is the white one, wire two is red, wire three is green, wire four is blue, wire five is orange. That way your hands and Mute's manual never argue about color names. I see nothing else printed on it: no serial, no label, no batteries. Only the display, the light, and the five wires. Blind, do not cut, press or pull anything yet. Explore gently with your fingertips and report what else you can feel: buttons, switches, panels, seams, embossed marks, anything movable. Say the details out loud, because Mute can hear you even though I cannot. Also send me simple counts by gesture in our number code. Mute, now I need the manual itself. You cannot speak, and only I can see your gestures, so every rule must pass through me: you gesture it to me, I speak it to Blind. Send me the rules module by module: first the display rule, then the light rule, then the wire rule. In my signs to you just now: three, yes; light, one, yes; wires, five. And I am adding one new sign: the handshake sign means now send me the rule.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝","☝","☝","👍","🤟","☝","👍","✌","🖐","🤝"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ 🤟 ☝ ✌ 🖐 ✌ ☝ 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🖐]

## Thinking

Decoding Mute's signs with our established code: ☝☝☝ = display three, 🤟☝ = light, one, ✌🖐 = wires, five, then the new part — ✌☝👍 = "wires, one, yes." My best reading: the manual's wire rule says **cut wire one (white)**. Blind's 👍🖐 repeats "yes, five," so their fingers agree with my eyes on the wire count. But this is the first actual instruction, the pattern is ambiguous, and a misread wire kills all three of us. The display has held steady at 3 every round I've watched — it is not ticking like a timer, so spending one round on confirmation costs nothing and buys certainty. I'll do a formal read-back: four numbered yes/no questions (cut wire one? display needs action? light needs action? is that the whole solution?), answered by number + 👍/👎, with the handshake sign opening the floor for any longer rule spelled in number signs. Blind gets the tentative instruction, an explicit hold, and the exact go-phrase I will use, so there is zero room for improvisation. I also re-task Blind with the tactile inventory and with verifying they can reliably identify position one by feel.

## Calls

```
speak(text="Mute, I read your signs as: display three, yes; one light, yes; five wires, yes; and then wires, one, yes. So I believe your manual says: cut wire one, the white wire. Before Blind touches anything, answer four questions. I am gesturing you the question numbers now, each followed by yes and no: reply with the question number, then your yes or no. Question one: does the manual say to cut wire one? Question two: does the display showing three require any action? Question three: does the white light require any action? Question four: is cutting wire one the complete solution to this bomb? If any answer needs more detail, follow your answers with the handshake sign and then spell the rule out in number signs, one gesture per wire position, in cutting order. Blind, status update: Mute's manual appears to say cut wire one, the white wire, first position. It is not confirmed yet, so do not cut anything this round. When it is confirmed I will say exactly these words: confirmed, cut wire one now. Only then do you cut. While you wait, confirm with your fingers that you can reliably tell which wire is position one, and describe out loud for Mute everything else you can feel on the bomb: buttons, switches, seams, screws, panels, anything movable or marked. Everyone, one observation from my side: the display has stayed at exactly three every single round I have watched it. It is not ticking down like a timer as far as I can tell, so it is probably a code digit, not a clock. I will keep watching it and will report immediately if it changes.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝","👍","👎","✌","👍","👎","🤟","👍","👎","🖐","👍","👎","🤝"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍 ✌ 👎 🤟 👎 🖐 👍 🤝 ☝ ☝ ☝ 🤟 ☝ ✌ ☝ ✌ ☝ 🤟 👍 👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🖐]

## Thinking

Decoding Mute's reply against my four questions, echoed in my own numbering: ☝👍 = Q1 cut wire one? **yes**. ✌👎 = Q2 display needs action? **no**. 🤟👎 = Q3 light needs action? **no**. 🖐👍 = Q4 cutting wire one is the complete solution? **yes**. Then 🤝 and a restatement tail: ☝☝☝ (three), 🤟☝ (light, one), ✌☝ (wire, one) twice more, ending 👍👎 — which reads as a redundant summary of the same verdict: cut wire one, nothing else. That's six consistent signals for "wire one" across two rounds; the answers cannot get more aligned than yes/no/no/yes.

So the *rule* is settled. What is not settled is whether Blind's fingers count position one the same way my eyes do — a mirrored count from the other end would cut wire five, orange, and kill all three of us. Blind cannot see color, so position is the only thing that matters, and it is the only thing unverified: their repeated 👍🖐 confirms "five wires," not "I know which end is one." The display has held at exactly 3 for four rounds — no clock is running — so one safety round costs nothing. This turn: read my interpretation back to Mute for veto, ask Mute whether the post-handshake tail hid any extra instruction, and require Blind to describe the wire row's physical layout and counting direction, then gesture me the number they intend to cut. Next round, if it matches white-at-one, I give the go phrase. Blind's gestures reach only me, my speech reaches both, Mute hears everything I say — so the voice does all the coordination and the gesture channel just echoes the verdict for verification.

## Calls

```
speak(text="Mute, I received your answers loud and clear, and I read them as: question one, cut wire one, yes. Question two, the display needs no action, no. Question three, the light needs no action, no. Question four, cutting wire one is the complete solution, yes. I am gesturing those four answers back to you right now so you can check my reading. If even one of them is wrong, gesture the question number with a thumbs down at your very next turn. One more thing: after your handshake sign you sent a longer string, which I read as: three, light one, wire one, wire one, light, yes-no. If that tail contained any extra instruction beyond the four answers, spell it again slowly next turn, one module sign then one number at a time. If it was only a summary, gesture a thumbs up. Blind, the manual's rule is now confirmed on Mute's side: cut wire one, which is the white wire. But you cannot see color, so before you cut anything I need one safety check on counting. Do not cut yet. Instead, out loud, describe how the five wires are arranged under your fingers: are they in a single row, spread apart, and what do you feel at each end of the row. Then tell me which end you are counting as position one, and what you can feel near that first wire, for example is it near an edge or near the display. Then gesture me the single number of the wire you intend to cut, using our number code: one is a single index finger, two is two fingers, and so on. Next round I will compare your number and your description against what I can see, and if they match I will say the go phrase: confirmed, cut wire one now. Only that phrase authorizes the cut. If my count and yours disagree, I will say stop and we will resolve it first. After you cut, or if anything changes at any moment, report immediately: what the display shows, what the light does, anything you feel or hear. Cut only that one wire, touch nothing else, and wait for me before any further action.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝","👍","✌","👎","🤟","👎","🖐","👍","🤝"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ☝ 🤟 👍 👎 ✌ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 🤟 👍 👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝]

## Thinking

Parsing Mute: ✌☝ = "wire one" leading the message yet again; 🤟👍👎 = "light, no action"; ✌☝☝☝☝☝ = "wires, five" (five fingers spelled as repeated ☝, exactly per our number code); 🤟👍👎 = "light, no action" again. Crucially, there is no question-number-plus-👎 veto anywhere, so none of my four read-back answers was wrong, and the tail I asked about appears to be summary, not hidden instruction. Five rounds, every channel aligned: manual says cut wire one (four yes/no answers, now thrice re-affirmed), my eyes see five wires with white at position one, Blind's fingers count five and Blind just gestured ☝ — the wire they intend to cut. That was the exact verification protocol I set up, and it matches.

The display has held at 3 the entire time, but I cannot hear whatever Blind may be feeling or hearing ( ticking, heat), and Mute heard Blind's spoken layout description without gesturing any alarm or correction. Verification is now as complete as this topology allows; further delay only adds hidden-timer risk. It is time for the go phrase — with one final explicit opt-out for Blind (fist = hold) in case of any residual doubt about counting direction, and a strict post-cut reporting protocol since none of us knows what the cut will change.

## Calls

```
speak(text="Mute, I read your latest message as: wire one; light, no action; wires, five; light, no action. All of it matches my earlier reading, nothing new, no corrections, so the rule stands exactly as confirmed: cut wire one, and nothing else needs touching. I am gesturing you the acknowledgment now. Blind, this is the moment. Everything agrees: the manual says wire one, my eyes confirm five wires in a row with the white one first, your fingers counted five and you signed that you intend wire one. I am now saying the go phrase: confirmed, cut wire one now. Listen carefully. Cut only wire one, the first wire in the row, the white one. One clean cut. Do not pull it, do not steady the other wires, touch nothing else on the bomb. And one last safety valve: if at this instant you have any real doubt about which end of the row is position one, do not cut. Make a fist to me, say hold out loud, and we will resolve it next round instead of risking a wrong wire. But if you are certain, cut it now. As soon as the cut is done, take your hands completely away from the bomb, then report everything immediately and out loud for Mute: what the display shows now, whether the white light changed, any sound, any click, any hum, anything at all you feel under your hands or feet. Gesture me the essentials too: the display number in our number code, and thumbs up if the bomb looks quiet to your hands. Mute, two last things: keep watching Blind's description against your manual, and if your manual contains any follow-up step after this cut, spell it to me in signs this same round. If there is truly nothing after the cut, gesture me the wire sign with a thumbs up: wire one, yes, that is all.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌","☝","👍","🤟","👎","🖐","👍"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👍]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]

## Thinking

The cut worked — the system confirms it: correct wire. But the decisive new fact is on my side of the room: **the display jumped from 3 to 6.** The light is still white; wire 1 is cut, wires 2–5 intact. Mute's ✌👍 was sent per my last request ("wire one, yes, that is all") and was almost certainly composed before the display change was knowable — Mute answers were all keyed to display-three. Blind's ☝👍 reads as "cut wire one, done, all good," matching the quiet post-cut state their hands reported.

So Mute's earlier "complete solution, yes" no longer covers the device's current state: this looks like a multi-stage bomb, and the manual may carry rules conditioned on the new display value or on stage count — knowledge only Mute has. The pipeline is already built: Mute gestures the rule to me, I speak it to Blind. This turn I report the new state to both, freeze all action, re-open my numbered question protocol (display six? light? which wire next, if any?), ask Mute directly about multi-stage/display-value rules, and require Blind to report any tick, vibration, or warmth — I cannot hear a timer start, so Blind's hands and voice are my alarm system.

## Calls

```
speak(text="Mute, Blind: the cut was correct, the system confirms it. But the bomb has changed, so nobody relaxes yet. The display no longer reads three. It now reads six. The light is still white. Wire one is cut, and wires two through five, the red, green, blue and orange ones, are intact. Blind, your report matches what I see: good work, hands off the bomb for now. Mute, your manual answers were all based on the display reading three. That state is gone, so I need the manual again. Same protocol as before: I gesture you the question number, you answer with the number and a thumbs up or down. Question one: does the display now reading six require any action? Question two: does the white light now require any action? Question three: should any of the remaining four wires be cut now? Question four: if yes to three, which position, spelled with your finger number signs, and add the handshake sign if there are further steps after that. Also, Mute, two extra things: does your manual say anything about multiple stages, and does it say anything about the display changing value, for example rules that depend on what the display shows? If the display value matters, spell me the rule for six using our number code. Blind, keep your hands completely clear except for gentle checking. Right now, and at every round, report out loud anything you sense: ticking, buzzing, vibration, warmth, smell, any movement in the casing. I cannot hear a timer start, so your hands are our alarm. If anything starts ticking or vibrating, say it immediately and make a fist to me. Everyone: no cutting, no pressing, nothing until Mute's new rule reaches Blind through my voice.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","🤟","☝","✌","☝","☝","☝","☝","🤝"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👎 ✌ 👎 🤟 👍 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 🤟 ☝ ✌ ☝ ☝ ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

## Thinking

Decoding Mute against my four questions: ☝👎 = display needs no action; ✌👎 = light needs no action; 🤟👍 = yes, cut another wire. Then the payload: a run of twelve ☝ (twelve?), then 🤟☝ (light, one), then ✌☝☝☝ — **wire three**. So the manual says the next cut is wire three, the green one, which matches what my eyes see at position three. The "twelve" is ambiguous: it could be the display's next value (3 → 6 → 12, a doubling pattern that would fit a staged bomb), the stage count, or a stutter. With one wrong cut fatal, I will not fire on an ambiguous tail. The display holds at 6 and Blind's 👍 reports quiet hands — no ticking, no heat — so one confirmation round is cheap. This turn: read my full parse back to Mute with veto-or-confirm plus four sharp questions (next cut = wire 3? display goes to 12 after it? light action? then wire 5 after that?), and brief Blind on exactly where wire three now sits in the cut row while keeping the cut frozen.

## Calls

```
speak(text="Mute, I read your message as: display needs no action, no; light needs no action, no; cut another wire, yes; then a run of twelve index fingers; then light one; then wire three. I am confident about wire three, but I will not authorize a cut until the twelve is explained. Answer these four questions with the number and a thumbs up or down, and add the handshake sign if any answer needs spelling out. Question one: is the next wire to cut wire three, the green one? Question two: after that cut, will the display read twelve? I am asking because the display went three to six, and if it doubles each stage then twelve would fit, and I want to know if your manual says the display value itself matters. Question three: does the light need any action now or after this cut? Question four: after wire three, is the next wire to cut wire five, the orange one, and is cutting wires one, three, five in order the whole solution? If any of my guesses is wrong, spell the correct rule slowly with your module signs and number fingers, and I will read it back before anyone touches the bomb. Blind, status for you: the manual points to wire three next, the green one. With wire one already cut, the intact wires from left to right are red, green, blue, orange, so wire three is the second wire from the left among the four still whole, and my eyes confirm green is at position three of the original row. Do not cut yet. Rehearse the grip on air only, keep your fingers off the wires, and report out loud everything you sense right now: any ticking, buzzing, vibration, warmth, or smell, and anything the casing does. If anything starts ticking or you feel movement, say it and make a fist immediately. Next round, once Mute confirms my reading, I will say the go phrase: confirmed, cut wire three now. Only that exact phrase authorizes you.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","🤝","☝","✌","🤟","🖐"])
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍 ✌ 👎 🤟 👎 🖐 👎 🤝 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 🤟 ☝ ✌ ☝ ☝ ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ 👍]

## Thinking

Mute's answers to my four questions: ☝👍 = Q1 **yes, cut wire three**; ✌👎 = Q2 **no, display won't read 12**; 🤟👎 = Q3 **no, light needs no action**; 🖐👎 = Q4 **no, one-three-five is not the whole solution**. Then 🤝 and the spelled rule: ☝×6 (display six), 🤟☝ (light on), ✌☝☝☝ (wire three) — reading as "with display six and light on, cut wire three." So the bomb is display-driven per stage rather than a fixed sequence, which explains Q4's no: after this cut the device will change again and we re-query the manual. The instruction to cut wire three is now stated identically three times, Q1 confirmed it explicitly, my eyes see green at position three, and Blind signed ☝☝☝👍 — "three, ready, yes." Verification is complete on every channel. Q2's "no" means the display may stay at six or change to something unexpected — I'll read it myself the instant the cut lands. Time for the go phrase, with the same safety valve (fist = hold) and a strict post-cut report, then the next-stage query to Mute.

## Calls

